chapters.title: Chapter 6 — Words ending -cious and -tious
chapters.description: Words that end with a 'shus' sound spelt -cious or -tious; our examples show which fits.

meaning.definition: Very cruel and fierce, ready to hurt.
meaning.example: In the story, a vicious troll guarded the bridge.

meaning.definition: Very valuable or loved, and not to be wasted.
meaning.example: She kept the precious ring in a small box.

meaning.definition: Kind, polite and generous in the way you treat people.
meaning.example: The queen gave a gracious smile to the crowd.

meaning.definition: Having lots of room inside.
meaning.example: We moved into a spacious flat with big windows.

meaning.definition: Careful to avoid danger or problems.
meaning.example: The cautious cat crept slowly across the wall.

meaning.definition: Tasting or smelling very good.
meaning.example: The soup smelled delicious.

meaning.definition: Wanting very much to do well and achieve something.
meaning.example: The ambitious girl hopes to win the race.

meaning.definition: Full of the goodness that helps you grow and stay healthy.
meaning.example: Beans and carrots make a nutritious dinner.

meaning.definition: Feeling that something is not quite right.
meaning.example: The dog gave the new cat a suspicious sniff.

meaning.definition: Able to spread easily from one person to another.
meaning.example: Her laugh was so infectious that we all joined in.

chapters.title: Chapter 7 — Words ending -cial and -tial
chapters.description: Words that end with a 'shul' sound spelt -cial or -tial; our examples show which fits.

meaning.definition: Connected with meeting and spending time with other people.
meaning.example: The club holds a social evening every Friday.

meaning.definition: To do with buying, selling and business.
meaning.example: A commercial bakery makes bread for many shops.

meaning.definition: To do with the face.
meaning.example: His facial expression showed he was surprised.

meaning.definition: Extremely important, so that everything depends on it.
meaning.example: Practice is crucial if you want to play well.

meaning.definition: Approved by someone in charge.
meaning.example: The official start time is nine in the morning.

meaning.definition: Happening first, at the very beginning.
meaning.example: Our initial plan was to walk to the park.

meaning.definition: Not complete; only a part of the whole.
meaning.example: We only had a partial view of the stage.

meaning.definition: Absolutely needed; you cannot do without it.
meaning.example: Water is essential for all living things.

meaning.definition: What someone or something could become with time.
meaning.example: The young player has great potential.

meaning.definition: Made by people, not found in nature.
meaning.example: The shop sold artificial flowers that never die.

chapters.title: Chapter 8 — Words ending -ant, -ance and -ancy
chapters.description: Words ending in -ant, -ance or -ancy, where the vowel sound is hard to hear; our examples show the rule.

meaning.definition: Far away in space or time.
meaning.example: We could see distant hills through the mist.

meaning.definition: Happening straight away, with no waiting.
meaning.example: The magic trick was an instant success.

meaning.definition: Nice, enjoyable and friendly.
meaning.example: We spent a pleasant afternoon by the river.

meaning.definition: Graceful and stylish in the way it looks.
meaning.example: The swan looked elegant as it glided past.

meaning.definition: Very clever, or extremely bright and shining.
meaning.example: The brilliant sunshine lit up the whole beach.

meaning.definition: The amount of space between two places.
meaning.example: The distance from here to school is a mile.

meaning.definition: Staying steady without falling over.
meaning.example: She kept her balance on the narrow wall.

meaning.definition: How much something matters.
meaning.example: The teacher explained the importance of good manners.

meaning.definition: How often someone is present, for example at school.
meaning.example: Our class had the best attendance this term.

meaning.definition: A job or room that is free and not yet taken.
meaning.example: The hotel had a vacancy for one night.

chapters.title: Chapter 9 — Words ending -able and -ably
chapters.description: Words ending in -able or -ably, which are often added to a whole word; our examples show the rule.

meaning.definition: Worth a lot of money or very useful.
meaning.example: The museum keeps a valuable painting in a glass case.

meaning.definition: So sweet and lovely that everyone wants to cuddle it.
meaning.example: The adorable puppy wagged its tail.

meaning.definition: In a way that is surprising and worth noticing.
meaning.example: The tiny boat was remarkably fast.

meaning.definition: Giving you pleasure and fun.
meaning.example: We had an enjoyable day at the seaside.

meaning.definition: Fair and sensible.
meaning.example: It is reasonable to ask for a turn.

meaning.definition: Easy to see or spot.
meaning.example: There was a noticeable crack in the old cup.

meaning.definition: Soft and relaxing, so that you feel at ease.
meaning.example: The sofa was big and comfortable.

meaning.definition: Popular and in style at the moment.
meaning.example: She wore a fashionable hat to the party.

meaning.definition: In a relaxed way, feeling at ease.
meaning.example: The cat slept comfortably on the warm rug.

meaning.definition: In a fair and sensible way.
meaning.example: The new bike was reasonably cheap.

chapters.title: Chapter 10 — Adding endings to words ending -fer
chapters.description: Words built on refer, prefer and transfer: whether the r doubles depends on where the stress falls; our examples show this.

meaning.definition: The person who makes sure players keep to the rules.
meaning.example: The referee blew the whistle at half time.

meaning.definition: To like one thing better than another.
meaning.example: I prefer toast to cereal.

meaning.definition: A mention of something, or a note of where to look.
meaning.example: The teacher made a reference to our trip.

meaning.definition: Liking one thing better than another.
meaning.example: Her preference is for blue rather than green.

meaning.definition: Mentioned something or pointed someone to it.
meaning.example: He referred to his notes during the talk.

meaning.definition: Mentioning something or pointing someone to it.
meaning.example: She is referring to the last chapter.

meaning.definition: Liked one thing better than another.
meaning.example: We preferred the red kite to the green one.

meaning.definition: Liking one thing better than another.
meaning.example: Preferring the quiet seat, he sat by the window.

meaning.definition: Moved from one place or person to another.
meaning.example: The photos were transferred onto the new computer.

meaning.definition: Moving something from one place or person to another.
meaning.example: Dad is transferring the water into a jug.
